subject: FluxHealth - 3yr commitment request: price lock + uplift-floor/renewal shield
body:
From: Kira Thompson <kira@fluxhealth.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: FluxHealth proposal — 3yr commitment, price lock and renewal protection

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. FluxHealth is ready to move forward on a 3-year committed contract if we can land a couple of commercial protections that are important for our budgeting:

- Price lock on selected model tiers for the full 36 months (no mid-term increases).
- Annual uplift cap of 3% (we'd accept CPI-based indexing but would like to cap at 3%).
- A renewal protection clause that limits any renewal-year increase to no more than 5% year-over-year and gives FluxHealth the right to terminate at renewal if the new renewal price exceeds that threshold.

I've attached a draft SOW and pricing spreadsheet for reference. We are offering a firm 3yr commitment at the ARR levels in the spreadsheet and would like to close before EOD Nov 12 if possible.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can sign up to those protections, or what executive approvals we need?

Best,
Kira Thompson
VP Product Operations
FluxHealth

---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Kira Thompson <kira@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FluxHealth proposal — 3yr commitment, price lock and renewal protection

Kira — thanks, this is clear and actionable.

Marissa (AE) — looping you in; we have the commitment but FluxHealth is asking for three non-standard items: multiyear price lock, low uplift cap (3%), and an explicit renewal termination right if renewal >5%.

I think the revenue and strategic value are there but these are outside standard playbook. Two asks for you all:
1) Marissa — can you confirm the final ARR & discount band we'll give under the 3yr? I penciled a 20% list discount at the volumes in the spreadsheet but let's confirm.
2) Markus/Monica — need exec / legal sign-off for the uplift/renewal language. Can we get guidance on whether finance/legal would consider a hybrid approach (e.g., price lock for first 24 months + annual uplift in year 3 only)?

Goal: return to Kira with a clear green/red and proposed contract language by Thu EOD.

Cheers,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: FluxHealth_SOW_Draft_v3.pdf

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com; markus_klein@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FluxHealth proposal — 3yr commitment, price lock and renewal protection

Folks — quick context and recommended commercials:

- FluxHealth proposed ARR: $1.2M (year 1), scale targets baked in across years 2–3.
- Standard Redwood 3yr pricing adds a 15% committed discount w/ annual CPI uplift; FluxHealth is requesting a stronger lock and lower uplift cap.

My recommendation (to balance risk):
1) Offer a 36-month price lock on the nominated model tier pricing for months 1–24.
2) Allow a one-time uplift in year 3 capped at 4.5% (instead of their requested 3%).
3) For renewal protection: include a clause that limits renewal increases to max 6% YoY and give FluxHealth a 90-day notice + a termination right if renewal exceeds 6%.
4) Add an uplift-floor clause for us (new here): if Redwood's incremental infra costs increase >12% YoY (measured by a published cost index we mutually agree to), Redwood reserves the right to renegotiate or apply a one-time surcharge capped at 6%.

Why: keeps revenue predictability for the customer while protecting Redwood against outsized infra cost shock.

What I need from Markus/Monica:
- Approval to agree to a 24-month strict lock + year-3 capped uplift at 4.5% (commercial exception).
- Legal sign-off on the renewal termination mechanics and the uplift-floor event language.

If approved, I'll return to Kira with the compromise and updated SOW.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive

---

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com; rafael_mendes@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 13:44:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FluxHealth proposal — 3yr commitment, price lock and renewal protection

Marissa — thanks for the write-up. A few finance-level notes before we commit:

- The 24-month lock + 4.5% year-3 uplift seems tolerable given the deal size, but the renewal cap of 6% is high for us to guarantee without an indexed floor. If we cap renewal increases we need a mechanism to protect against multi-year hardware inflation or changes in model compute intensity (e.g., if they move to larger sequence lengths or higher QPS).

- Suggest tightening the uplift-floor trigger: use a public cloud GPU price index + Redwood infra ops CAGR threshold (we can propose the exact index). If that trigger fires, the remediation should be a negotiated surcharge or a right to exit, not an automatic surcharge.

- Require deal to include a minimum annual commit usage (token or compute threshold) to avoid revenue downside.

Conclusion: I provisionally approve the commercial exception (24m lock + year-3 uplift cap 4.5%) subject to:
1) Legal-approved uplift-floor language that uses a clear index and negotiated remediation path.
2) Minimum committed usage metric in the SOW.
3) Exec notification/OK from VP Commercial for anything that grants a renewal termination right tied to price.

Monica — can Legal draft redline suggestions for the renewal/termination and uplift-floor clauses? If we can get those before Thu EOD, I'll take it up the chain.

-Markus
SVP Finance, Redwood Inference

---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com; rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FluxHealth proposal — 3yr commitment, price lock and renewal protection

Team — attached are two suggested redlines: one for the renewal protection section and one for the uplift-floor. High level:

- Renewal protection: replace an unconditional termination right with a market-remedy clause. Example language: "At renewal, if Redwood's offered renewal price exceeds the Renewal Cap (6%), Customer may elect a 60-day negotiation period to return to agreement on price adjustments; if parties cannot agree, Customer may terminate with 30 days' notice."

- Uplift-floor trigger: specify the exact indices (e.g., Nvidia GPU public spot index + DC power CPI index), require written notice and a 30-day remediation negotiation, and cap any one-time surcharge at 6%. No automatic surcharges.

I also flagged that the SOW must include minimum committed usage by quarter and an audit right to validate usage.

I'll circulate a cleaned up SOW with inline redlines within 2 hours. If you want Legal to propose the exact index list, I can include it but would need approval from Ops to verify indices are meaningful.

-Monica
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial

Attachment: FluxHealth_MA-terms.docx

---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Kira Thompson <kira@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com; markus_klein@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FluxHealth proposal — 3yr commitment, price lock and renewal protection

Kira — thanks for the fast turnaround. Quick update from our side:

- We can offer a compromise: strict price lock for months 1–24; a single capped uplift in year 3 (4.5%); renewal cap language to be drafted (target Renewal Cap: 6% with a 60-day negotiation remediation and the right to terminate if no agreement is reached).
- Legal will propose exact wording for the uplift-floor trigger and remediation — to be sent to you shortly; it includes a requirement of a minimum committed usage metric in the SOW.
- Next steps: Marissa will update the SOW with the revised financials and the redlined clauses and will get back to you with the final SOW + DocuSign link for signature.

If that works, can you confirm acceptance of the approach by Fri EOD so we can lock the discount pricing?

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: FluxHealth_PRICING_LINEITEMS.xlsx
